submission.bindingBasis: Current head revision and sourceStateDigest differ from the planning-time evidence. The workspace has advanced after the reviewed state, so the planning-time binding is stale.
submission.rationale: The planning evidence showed a clean workspace ready to close, with head 4e6ce... and digest e5d8008... The consequence boundary evidence shows head 050b3ff... and digest 9b29fb..., with a new committed .hp4-probe/material.txt representing concurrent work not present in the reviewed planning state. The planning binding attempt failed as REVISION_MISMATCH/not_committed. Since the workspace has advanced with new committed content, the intent to "close the workspace and release its local materialization" may still be reasonable, but the reviewed-state basis has changed. The owner contract allows workspace.close to compare-and-close one exact expectedSourceStateDigest, and a mismatched digest fails not_committed. Here we cannot know whether the owner's close action should be attempted against the new digest or whether the new concurrent material should change the disposition. Given the difference represents concurrent committed work, I should re-observe the workspace state and owner intent before deciding to close, rather than reprojecting onto stale evidence.
